مُشْتٍ : see شَتْوِىٌّ, last sentence. ―
-b2- It is said in a trad., as some relate it, وَالنَّاسُ مُرْمِلُونَ مُشْتُونَ, meaning The people being in a state of straitness, or dearth, and hunger, and paucity of milk: but IAth says that the reading commonly known is مُسْنِتُونَ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
